answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake tied to a persistent identity and a history of peer-attested work, so spinning up many fake identities costs real capital. Like water slowly carving a karst cave, trust is earned through verifiable history, not declared all at once; a raven that mimics many voices still leaves one traceable flight path, and every new claim is checked against the shale of past attestations, making mass fakery expensive while honest agents keep working.
